approval_time_estimate: Instant for personal accounts; 2–5 days for organizational access
summary: Microsoft Azure AD / Entra ID OAuth (used for Outlook, OneDrive, Teams, and all Microsoft 365 services) is well-documented and works immediately for personal Microsoft accounts. Access to organizational (work/school) accounts requires tenant admin consent for certain scopes, which can add complexity. The Azure portal setup is comprehensive but has more steps than simpler providers. Composio provides managed auth for Microsoft services.
key_facts: Personal Microsoft accounts can be connected immediately after app registration
Work/school accounts may require tenant admin consent for some scopes
App registration in Azure Portal (Entra ID) is self-service and immediate
Multi-tenant apps (personal + work accounts) require careful configuration
Some Graph API scopes require admin consent by default
Composio managed auth available for prototyping
Publisher verification badge helps build trust with enterprise users

steps.title: Register App in Azure Portal
steps.description: Go to portal.azure.com → Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → New registration. Fill in app name. Under 'Supported account types', select 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' for the broadest reach. Add your redirect URI.
warnings: Account type selection cannot be easily changed later — choose carefully

steps.title: Add Redirect URI
steps.description: In the app's Authentication section, add platform 'Web' and redirect URI: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Enable 'Access tokens' and 'ID tokens' under Implicit grant if needed.

steps.title: Configure API Permissions
steps.description: Go to API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph. Add delegated permissions for your use case: Mail.Read, Calendars.Read, Files.Read, User.Read, etc. Note which scopes require admin consent (shown with shield icon).
warnings: Admin consent required scopes (like Mail.ReadWrite for all users) will block enterprise users until their tenant admin approves
Use the least privileged scopes possible

steps.title: Create Client Secret
steps.description: Go to Certificates & secrets → New client secret. Set an expiration (max 24 months). Copy the secret value immediately — it's only shown once. Note the Application (client) ID from the Overview page.
warnings: Set a calendar reminder to rotate secrets before they expire — expired secrets break your integration

steps.title: Configure in Composio
steps.description: Use the Application (client) ID as Client ID and your client secret value. The tenant ID for multi-tenant apps is 'common'. Configure Composio custom auth config with toolkit='microsoft' (or specific toolkit like 'outlook').

requirements.account_type: Free Microsoft account (personal) or Azure account (organizational apps)

blockers.title: Admin Consent for Organizational Scopes
blockers.description: Many Microsoft Graph scopes for reading org-level data require tenant admin consent. Individual users cannot grant these — their org's IT admin must approve your app for their tenant.
blockers.workaround: Stick to user-delegated scopes where possible. For scopes requiring admin consent, provide a separate admin consent URL that tenant admins can use to pre-approve your app.

blockers.title: Client Secret Expiration
blockers.description: Azure client secrets expire (max 24 months). When they expire, your integration breaks for all users.
blockers.workaround: Use certificate-based authentication instead for production, or set up automated secret rotation with Azure Key Vault.
